<description>
{
 "summary": "Removes time-based mempool transaction eviction (`-mempoolexpiry`) and its associated multi_index container index. Transactions now only leave the mempool via block inclusion, replacement, conflict, or size-based eviction under `-maxmempool`. The configuration option `-mempoolexpiry` is retained as a hidden no-op option that issues a warning when set.",
 "problem": "Evicting transactions purely based on age (previously defaulting to two weeks) drops transactions that remain incentive-compatible and mineable, such as low-feerate parents waiting on CPFP fee-bumping children. Maintaining the age-based index also imposes per-entry memory overhead for an eviction mechanism that conflicts with miner incentives.",
 "evidence": [
  "Fixes linked issue #33510 ('Mempool Expiry eviction might remove txs that could be mined in the next block')",
  "Author description and commit message note eviction by age is incentive-incompatible and can drop still-mineable transactions waiting on child fee bumps",
  "Author description highlights secondary memory savings: 'removing it saves an ordered-tree node per mempool entry... within the same -maxmempool budget the mempool fits slightly more transactions'"
 ],

<category name="mempool" title="Mempool and policy">
## Covers

Which unconfirmed transactions the node accepts, keeps, and relays:
standardness and policy rules, replacement rules, package acceptance
and relay, mempool data structures and limits, eviction, fee
estimation, and the cluster mempool project. The Mempool and TX fees
and policy labels are a strong prior.

Not mempool: consensus validity (validation); block template
construction (mining); the p2p messages that carry transactions (p2p).

## What matters here

Denial-of-service and pinning resistance first: policy is the node's
defense against transactions designed to waste resources or to block
legitimate replacements, and second-layer protocols depend on it. Then
correctness of acceptance and replacement rules against their stated
specifications, since wallets and Lightning implementations build on
them. Then progress on the cluster mempool project and the improvements
it unblocks. Then fee estimation accuracy, which every wallet user
feels. Then memory and CPU behavior under load.

Policy changes with a written rationale and downstream demand rank
above local tidy-ups.
